title: six playable characters, a picker, and the crowds built from the six (cast A)
lensAText: a sceptical game art director and UX lead. For each of the six, open the reference sheets in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/characters/0N-name/ (body-sheet.webp, face-sheet.webp) with the Read tool and compare them with the builder's renders view by view: is each character clearly recognisable as THAT person (build and height, skin tone, face shape, hair, outfit and colours, accessories), consistent with the others in style, readable at phone size, free of artefacts (gaps, clipping, z-fighting, broken hair or cloth)? Then take your own frames in ONE short Playwright script on dist/artifact.html: the picker at 390x844 (phone viewport copy, DPR 3) and 1450x767; pick two different characters, walk in Lot 57 and Stoppage Time (via Go To, Get out) and confirm the chosen one is the one on screen and the driving hands take their skin tone.
brief: THE OWNER (2026-11-11 ~12:30 PM PT): "make there be 6 characters to choose from 3 being male and 3 female that ChatGPT can generate images for you to accurately and realistically use for this game" (later: 'realistically' means usable, not photoreal). The owner generated the reference sheets: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/characters/ (roster.md has the names, ages, builds, outfits and notes; each 0N-name/ folder has body-sheet.webp = front/three-quarter/side/back A-pose and face-sheet.webp = front/profile/three-quarter smile). The six: 01 Mateo Reyes (27, 175 cm, stocky), 02 Danny Tran (31, 172 cm, slim, glasses), 03 Marcus Bell (38, 188 cm, muscular, shaved head, beard, scar on his RIGHT eyebrow, sunglasses on head), 04 Leila Farahani (29, 168 cm, wavy shoulder-length hair, hoops, blazer), 05 Jas Cruz (24, 160 cm, high ponytail, cropped bomber), 06 Kate Morgan (35, 175 cm, freckles, low ponytail, denim shirt, cargo pants). BUILD: (1) src/onfoot/cast.ts (new, ours): the six as presets for the existing people builder (src/onfoot/people: buildPerson, preset, PRESETS, PersonOptions, Look, Garment, Accessories), matching the sheets as closely as the stylised real-time look allows (honest: stylised 3D on a phone, not photoreal). (2) Missing builder features, ADDITIVE ONLY, in src/onfoot/people/* (agreed with the session that owns it): new hair styles (high ponytail, low ponytail, skin fade with textured top, side-part undercut, shoulder-length waves), garments (bomber, blazer, overshirt, work jacket, henley, cargo pants, chino shorts, work pants, sandals, deck shoes, low heels, chunky sneakers, boots) and accessories (glasses, sunglasses on the head, thin chain, hoop earrings, watch, hair tie) behind NEW parameter values; existing defaults, presets and the public API unchanged; avoid face.ts, masks.ts and skin.ts (another branch changes them; if a face feature truly needs them, say so instead). (3) A character picker: in the main menu or garage, six cards with each character's three-quarter smile portrait (cropped from face-sheet.webp, compressed WebP at most ~40 KB each, inlined) plus a live 3D turntable of the selected one; the choice is saved in the profile; default = keep today's player look until the player picks. (4) The chosen character is the player's avatar on foot in Lot 57 and Stoppage Time (inside the game through src/onfoot/embed.ts, and the standalone pages), and the driving hands take their skin tone through the hands' public setTone(hex) (no edits to src/preview/hands*). Phone-cheap: LOD via the builder's own budget; no per-frame allocation. Our own names; no real brands or logos on clothing. ADD a regression check: the six presets build within budget, the picker saves and restores the choice, the venue avatar matches the choice, the hands' tone follows. PROVE: npx tsc --noEmit; npm run build (owner-test mark kept); npm test -- --only=boot,phone,venues and the new check; renders of each character front/side/back beside the same views cropped from its body sheet, and the head beside the face sheet, into tests/out/cast/; picker frames at 390x844 and 1450x767; one frame of a chosen character in each venue. THE OWNER'S MASTER BRIEF (uploaded 2026-11-11 ~1:25 PM PT; read ALL of it: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/characters/MASTER_PROMPT.md) GOVERNS where it is more specific. Its IDs are technical labels; keep our names: M01 = Marcus Bell, M02 = Mateo Reyes, M03 = Danny Tran, F01 = Jas Cruz, F02 = Leila Farahani, F03 = Kate Morgan. Its 'nine PNGs' and character_roster.json were NOT attached (only the brief); we have MORE: a body sheet and a face sheet for all six (use them; do not claim any other file was inspected). Mismatches to record, not blend: Marcus's scar is on his RIGHT eyebrow in both images (text says left: follow the images); Mateo's jacket is drawn zip-front (text says open). THIS LANE (cast A) ADDS, per that brief: (5) ONE data-driven character catalog (cast.ts or a JSON it reads, in the project's own format): stable ID, name, portrait reference, the people-builder preset/params (our 'mesh and material references'), height and proportion data, wardrobe slots, animation config, unlock category ('base' for the six; 'pack' reserved). (6) NPC REUSE: the six are the ONLY human appearance archetypes for the current NPCs: rebuild Lot 57's and Stoppage Time's crowds and staff (src/onfoot/lot57/npcs.ts and crowd-worker.ts; src/onfoot/venues/sportsbar/crowd.ts, crew.ts, house.ts, life.ts; not people/*) from the six base looks with variety from wardrobe tints, compatible accessory choices, routes, schedules, idle and conversation timing, keeping each face, skin tone, defining hair and proportions recognisable, and avoid identical copies side by side; keep the crowd budgets, LODs and pooling. Honest labels ('Simulated crowd') stay. (7) A FUTURE TWO-CHARACTER PACK scaffold only: one catalog entry in src/store/catalog.json for a pair (one man, one woman), available: false, ONE configurable price with a caveat that the final price is undecided ($5 or $10 for the pair), a 'pack' unlock category in the cast catalog with NO identities shipped and nothing in the NPC pool; the store stays in test mode. (8) Write PROJECT_OC_CAST.md: the catalog and asset status (what exists: procedural presets, no imported meshes; missing pieces), mismatches, what this lane changed, verified results, the highest-impact remaining visual defects, and the next task (cast B: the full drive-park-exit-walk-enter-interact-leave-drive-reload loop and a graphics pass on the six). Extra proof for these: frames of each venue's crowd showing the six-look variety at 1280x720; the regression check also asserts the NPC pool only uses the six base looks and the pack is not for sale.
